entries.note: The passage uses insults to explain his fear. The normalization turns that personal explanation into a causal claim about danger.

entries.test: Public tests and documented outputs showing whether contemporary GPT systems reliably reject falsehoods or instead generate and spread unverified false claims would test this assertion.
entries.note: The plain reading concerns unreliable filtering, rather than an inability to reject any false statement.

entries.test: Public evaluations and scientific results involving GPT-5, together with records of whether interstellar starships existed in 2024, would test these predictions.
entries.note: The 2024 deadline applies to starships, not explicitly to fusion or nanotechnology.

entries.test: GPT-4 chess results and playing-strength comparisons with documented 1978 chess computers would settle the comparison.
Public evidence of GPT-5 enabling interstellar spacecraft or an unbeatable military capability would contradict the prediction.
entries.note: The source says anyone, including actors other than countries; the normalization narrows that scope.
The singularity has no sufficiently shared operational meaning here.
“A safe bet” presents a probable outcome; the normalization removes that qualification.

entries.test: Blinded human comparisons of GPT-5 and GPT-4 prose generated from matched prompts would test which produces more convincing prose.
Marcus's published predictions about persistent GPT-4 flaws, compared with public GPT-4 evaluations, would establish whether every predicted flaw persisted.
Documented, independently validated novel scientific findings generated by contemporary standalone GPT models would test the assertion.
entries.note: The standalone condition matters; discoveries by larger tool-assisted systems would not directly settle it.

entries.test: Public evaluations demonstrating reliable factual verification by standalone GPT models would contradict the asserted limitation.
entries.note: “Forte” means a strength, not necessarily the task at which models are best. The surrounding paragraph concerns GPT models on their own.

entries.test: Publicly documented GPT-generated ideas independently established as novel rather than reproductions of existing ideas would test this assertion.

entries.note: The prediction about LLMs is conditional on transformative AI emerging. “A tiny part” supplies no shared way to measure architectural or causal contribution.
The passage gives no shared standard for the intelligence being overattributed or the degree that makes expectations fantasies.
The source explains how misconceptions generate expectations; the normalization drops that causal claim and generalizes the feats described. “Real understanding” has no agreed test here.

entries.test: Repeated public evaluations of GPT-4 across tasks, including summarization, would show whether reported successes reproduce reliably.
entries.note: In context, replicability concerns repeatable task success, not identical wording.

entries.test: Independent replications and robust evaluations of the cognitive abilities publicly attributed to GPT-4 at publication would test whether essentially none withstand scrutiny.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion identifies theory of mind, reasoning, and related cognitive evaluations.

entries.test: Public theory-of-mind evaluations of contemporary LLMs, including controlled variations and independent replications, would test whether they demonstrate robust mastery.
entries.note: Marcus explicitly endorses the conclusion attributed to Sap's investigation.

entries.test: Public performance and deployment evidence for GPT in data processing, autonomous driving, and tracking airborne military aircraft would test these capability claims.
entries.note: The passage mixes a current limitation with future predictions. The normalization changes the tracking prediction to the present and drops “in flight.”
The source questions how much users ought to trust summaries in critical applications. The normalization also drops the proposed video's speed and volume requirements and adds “only.”

entries.test: Public planning benchmarks and military task evaluations would test whether contemporary GPT planning failures prevent successful use in almost all military scenarios.
entries.note: The claim links a planning limitation to military unsuitability.

entries.test: Publicly documented defense or security applications with demonstrable effects attributable to GPT-5 would establish some impact.
entries.note: “I don’t doubt” expresses firm expectation.

entries.test: Public records of GPT-5 availability and any GPT-5-driven transformation of US or Chinese capabilities during Q4 2023 would test the prediction.
entries.note: The normalization turns “still seems like a fantasy to me” into an unqualified denial. The dated prediction nevertheless has a testable core.
